caption: The public Pricing Plans page of Easy-Peasy.AI as seen logged out (the Log in and Sign up buttons are in the top bar): the line 100% no risk, 30-day money back guarantee., the switch Monthly billing and Yearly billing -50% (yearly selected), and the first row of plan cards Free ($0/month), Starter ($8/month, billed yearly $192 $96), Unlimited 50 ($12/month, $288 $144) and Unlimited ($16.5/month, $384 $198, Most popular), each with a Start button. The tester had covered the lower left corner with black; it is covered again with magenta.

The Choose your plan window that opened after the click on Regenerate with Advanced AI, with the text Your plan has reached its word limit. To continue, please upgrade your plan. and the Monthly and Yearly switch (yearly selected). It shows four paid plans and no Free plan: Starter $8 (billed yearly $192 $96), Unlimited 50 $12 ($288 $144), Unlimited $16.5 ($384 $198, Most popular) and Unlimited 200 $28 ($576 $336), with their allowances such as 25,000 Opus or 50,000 Sonnet, GPT-5, Gemini Pro words and 200 image/video credits for Starter, and 200,000 Opus or 400,000 Sonnet words, 750 credits, Unlimited Transcriptions, 120,000 characters Text-to-Speech and 8 Bots for Unlimited 200. The AI Images page (Image Generator) after one image was made: the prompt about a modern minimalist solar-powered desk lamp on a wooden desk, the generated product image of a white desk lamp with a small solar panel on top, the counter 0 credits with an Upgrade button, and the notice You're out of image credits. Upgrade your plan to keep creating. The image shows no panel for the wireless charging pad that the prompt of the blog post spoke about. A magenta patch masks the lower left corner.
